Bed Scam - Kids Dreams Dashed

By: Graham Coetzer | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We investigate an unscrupulous manufacturer who took money upfront from unsuspecting parents hoping to buy their children their dream beds - only to leave them in the lurch

Unique Selling Point:
To an adult a bed is just that, a bed. But to a young child, it represents so much more - a place of safety and comfort. We meet a group of angry parents who spent thousands of rands on custom beds for their toddlers, but months down the line they say the manufacturers, Angus and Lonita Davis from BEL Furniture Solutions have come up with nothing but empty promises.

Summary:
JP Sinden ordered a custom bed for his 5 year old daughter and paid R5400 to BEL in August last year. The bed was to be a birthday gift for her in September. He was promised delivery in 3 weeks.

Danielle Gun and Charlotte Espag also ordered and paid for beds at BEL - Charlotte for her 2 year old son and Danielle for their 5 year old son in June and September last year respectively. They are just three of the 17 cases that we know of, of people who have paid Angus and Lonita and not received their beds. Most of them have now waited months, and many of them have gone as far as laying criminal charges of theft with the police. They all accuse Angus and Lonita of running a complete scam.

Further information:
Except for our three case studies who are willing to talk to us on camera, we also have Dewald van Rensburg owner of Dewald's Toolbox, a company that also manufactures beds etc. He came across BEL when he realised that they were stealing images of his beds from his website and Facebook pages and using it as their own marketing material(We have screen grabs etc) After confronting Angus about it, he was threatened with lawyers etc. He's also given us whatsapp voice notes where Angus constantly swears at him etc, stuff like "Stop this childish fucking shit" etc.

We have also confirmed that Angus owns another company, BEL Balustrades, which also has a very poor record of delivering on their promises. In one of the whatsapp voice notes, Angus admits that BEL Balustrades is refunding people, but we have case studies who are still waiting.

All our bed case studies were promised refunds and or their beds by the end of December 2021 in a letter from Angus, which we have a copy of. He also throws his own wife under the bus in the letter, saying she made promises she could not keep. But to date none of our case studies have been refunded or received beds.

At the end of the day this is more than just a consumer story - what BEL is doing is essentially depriving children of their dreams.

We should be able to get a confront.

Script:


Bed Scammer
First Draft Script
08 Feb 2021

Sound Up Child Reading
Wherever your dreams take you when you’re asleep, unicorn will be there as your friend. Ready to enjoy all the wondrous places, hoping it will never quite end…

Voice
For most of us a bed is just a bed - a place to recover from the humdrum and rush of daily life. But for a child, a bed is about so much more - it could be a place to meet unicorns, or a magical castle - a safe space where imaginations can run wild.

Link Derek
You can imagine how excited a 5 year old girl would be getting a specially crafted hand built bed for her 5th birthday. It was a financial stretch for her parents, but she was worth it.

Sound Up JP Sinden
Jp: Yeah she’s a lovely kid. Into sports playing netball and tennis already.

Derek: The light of you and Riana’s lives?

Jp: Absolutely, absolutely.

Voice
This proud father is JP Sinden from Pretoria. And this is his 5-year-old daughter, Viandrie. She was at school the day we met her parents. There’s no doubt the fun-loving toddler is the apple of her father’s eye. Last year JP and his wife Riana wanted to spoil little Viandrie with a special birthday present – her very own custom-made bed.

Sound Up JP
Derek: And this was a big purchase for you?

JP: Yes, yes absolutely. I mean we’ve been promising this for her. In afrikaans she’s referring to her “huisie” bed, because it has a little house on the top and a slide…

Derek: Well I’m looking at a picture of the “huisie” bed here and wow it is quite a bed isn’t it, I mean you’ve got your living quarters upstairs, hey, entertainment area?

Jp: Absolutely.

Voice
Laura Bos, a mother of two from Johannesburg, was also looking for a toddler’ s bed last year for her two and a half year old son.

Sound Up Laura
And I thought for once let’s buy at a craftmanship shop, where it’s all home made and it looked very beautiful, and you know I get these ads on Instagram and Facebook.

Voice
Laura and JP found beds advertised on social media by this company, BEL Furniture. In its Spring Promotion Catalogue owners Angus and Lonita Davis described BEL as a small family-owned business where each piece of furniture was crafted by hand and guaranteed for at least 8 years.

Sound Up JP
Derek: Here’s the amount, R5400, how did you go about paying it?

JP: So on the last day of September we made the 50% deposit payment, which they required. And then on the following day we decided we have the money available so let’s pay the full amount.

Voice
But both JP and Laura say they never received their beds nor the refunds they requested.

Charlotte Espag from Thabazimbi also paid Bel Furniture R3800 upfront and she too never received her two year old son’s bed.

Sound Up Charlotte
We had to then go buy him another bed, and emotionally…I was pregnant at the time, i was 35 weeks pregnant. And you now find out that these people have taken you for a ride, and what do you do?

Voice
When Laura saw that her son’s R4300 bed was not forthcoming, she did a little online digging.

Sound Up Laura
And I saw there were some other angry ladies, angry mommies, who also reacted saying oh these are scammers, do not contact them and don’t order beds.

Voice
We’ve had complaints from no less than 18 BEL Furniture clients who all said they’d paid deposits without ever receiving their goods. And messages like these found on a whatsapp group they’d started highlight who the true victims are.

Sound Up female Voice reading whatsapp messages
I have not received my bed or a refund as requested. This was a christmas gift for my son from his grand parents. His first big boy bed.

Mine was for my son’s fourth birthday, had to buy another one, couldn’t deal with the disappointment.

Link Derek
With Bel Furniture Solutions it appears that what you see isn’t always what you get. In fact the images that you’re looking at aren’t even their own creations…

Sound Up Woodwork

Voice
Dewald van Rensburg runs a successful home furniture manufacturing business called Dewald’s Toolbox.

Sound Up Dewald
Derek: What do you offer?

Dewald: House beds, tepee beds, that’s my main line of product is these custom beds.

Voice
He markets his beds on Social Media

Sound Up Dewald
Derek: Then you noticed that some of your images were on other people’s Facebook pages and websites?

Dewald: Yes, it’s actually my clients who brought it to my attention.

Voice
His photos were being used by BEL Furniture and marketed as their own, priced cheaper than Dewald says he could ever make them.

Sound Up Dewald
That was September last year, that’s the first time it came to light. Told them to remove it. A week later we found a couple more, we contacted them again to tell them please remove the stuff.

Voice
But when it happened a third time, he took to social media with some choice posts.

Sound Up Dewald
Dewald: That’s when it started to become heated, the conversations.

Derek: Not exactly a cordial conversation?

Dewald: Ja, definitely not.

Derek: Should we listen to a few clips?

Dewald: Ja, that would be good.

Voice
This is an extract of a voice note Angus sent to Dewald about his Facebook posts.

Sound Up Angus REMEMBER TO BLEEP IN MIX PLEASE
And I need you, and if you don’t take that shit off fucking Facebook, trust me there will be shit.

Sound Up Dewald
Derek: So how did you react to that?

Dewald: We just basically told him, sorry, we cannot remove it. It’s sitting there for anyone to see. I am not calling you a scam, I’m saying you are using my stuff, and you’re not delivering that stuff and I’m not working for you.

Voice
We asked Angus and Lonita Davis for interviews, and Angus agreed to come and explain their side of the story. Angus said he did not own a factory where his beds were made, but instead contracted the work out to carpenters that he blames for not delivering on their promises.

Sound Up Angus
Derek: I mean you’re taking money in times that are tight and not delivering?

Angus: We have, we have delivered a few.

Derek: A few?

Angus: And we have refunded a couple of them…

Derek: A few?

Angus: Say about 40% of our clients that had already placed their orders by us.

Voice
So by his own admission, Angus has only delivered beds to or refunded fewer than half of his clients. It’s hard to tell, since not even Angus seems to know exactly how many people he owes money to…

Sound Up Angus
Derek: How many people do you owe money to and how much?

Angus: I can say about 20, 25, the new clients.

Derek: So you owe about 25 clients?

Angus: Round about. I haven’t got my, my invoice app has been offline since the middle of December because I haven’t paid them up so I couldn’t do my due diligence for this (unintelligible word).

Voice
Due diligence might have come in handy with their previous on-line business called Neverland Designs. That company, which also sold children’s beds, was also accused of being a scam.

Sound Up Angus
Derek: But that’s two online companies where you’ve been accused of scamming your clients. It’s not great is it?

Angus: No, it’s not. But we were under the impression we’re not going to make the same mistake again.

Voice
But at least some of the same mistakes have been made, and the angry parents we spoke to are not impressed.

Sound Up JP
If you take someone’s money, and you don’t deliver, you don’t communicate, and you are not getting your money back, that’s a scam. There’s no other word for it.

Voice
It doesn’t help that BEL Furniture weren’t posting their own products online…

Sound Up Angus
Derek: Why did you steal images say from Dewald?

Angus: I didn’t steal no images from Dewald, that’s the next question I’m going to put down my foot on(sic).

Derek: But you’ve used identical images, we’ve seen them?

Angus: That department I’m going to have to say, my wife is the one with the marketing.

Derek: Angus, these are the images you used, and these are Dewald’s. And obviously it’s a copy?

Angus: Ja that’s where I’m going to have to… this one I know of, this one, I didn’t do the marketing on this one.

Derek: You got quite fiery in your voice messages to Dewald?

Angus: No because I couldn’t understand where’s it coming from. I was just upset, that’s all.

Derek: I mean do you want to listen to what you said?

Angus: I know what I said.

Derek: You know what you said?

Angus: I know what I said.

Derek: You proud of it?

Angus: No, I’m not proud of it at all.

Voice
By the end of our interview Angus Davis promised to pay back all his clients before the end of this month. He would sell furniture online no more. The experience had clearly been an emotional one.

Sound Up Angus
Derek: I just hope firstly that you can sort your life out, and repay you know these people that you are promising to repay.

Angus: That’s what I want to say Derek, to all the clients that I need to refund I can guarantee you that I’m going to do it.

Link Derek
Angus Davis says it never rains but it pours, he promises to repay all his clients in full and exit the online space entirely. But along the way he’s crushed a lot of childhood dreams.

AM PREF: Voice
Dreams like little Viandrie Sinden’s “huisie bed” … which she’s had to give up on.
















PROMOS

PROMO 1 (21SEC)

Sound Up Carpentry(4sec)

Voice
An angry group of parents who thought they were ordering their children the perfect homemade gift online

Sound Up JP
That’s a scam. There’s no other word for it.

Voice
We take a closer look at a case of bedtime blues…






PROMO 2 (21SEC)

Voice
From stolen IP…

Sound Up Dewald
Derek: Not exactly a cordial conversation?

Dewald: Ja, definitely not.

Derek: Should we listen to a few clips?

Dewald: Ja, that would be good.

Voice
To furious mothers…

Sound Up Laura
angry mommies, who also reacted saying oh these are scammers, do not contact them

Voice
We tell a different kind of bedtime story…






PROMO 3 (11 Sec)
A group of furious parents have accused one online retailer of not only taking their money and failing to deliver, but also breaking their children’s hearts.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We investigate an unscrupulous manufacturer who took money upfront from unsuspecting parents hoping to buy their children their dream beds - only to leave them in the lurch
metadata.Unique Selling Point: To an adult a bed is just that, a bed. But to a young child, it represents so much more - a place of safety and comfort. We meet a group of angry parents who spent thousands of rands on custom beds for their toddlers, but months down the line they say the manufacturers, Angus and Lonita Davis from BEL Furniture Solutions have come up with nothing but empty promises.
metadata.Summary: JP Sinden ordered a custom bed for his 5 year old daughter and paid R5400 to BEL in August last year. The bed was to be a birthday gift for her in September. He was promised delivery in 3 weeks. Danielle Gun and Charlotte Espag also ordered and paid for beds at BEL - Charlotte for her 2 year old son and Danielle for their 5 year old son in June and September last year respectively. They are just three of the 17 cases that we know of, of people who have paid Angus and Lonita and not received their beds. Most of them have now waited months, and many of them have gone as far as laying criminal charges of theft with the police. They all accuse Angus and Lonita of running a complete scam.
metadata.Further information: Except for our three case studies who are willing to talk to us on camera, we also have Dewald van Rensburg owner of Dewald's Toolbox, a company that also manufactures beds etc. He came across BEL when he realised that they were stealing images of his beds from his website and Facebook pages and using it as their own marketing material(We have screen grabs etc) After confronting Angus about it, he was threatened with lawyers etc. He's also given us whatsapp voice notes where Angus constantly swears at him etc, stuff like "Stop this childish fucking shit" etc. We have also confirmed that Angus owns another company, BEL Balustrades, which also has a very poor record of delivering on their promises. In one of the whatsapp voice notes, Angus admits that BEL Balustrades is refunding people, but we have case studies who are still waiting. All our bed case studies were promised refunds and or their beds by the end of December 2021 in a letter from Angus, which we have a copy of. He also throws his own wife under the bus in the letter, saying she made promises she could not keep. But to date none of our case studies have been refunded or received beds. At the end of the day this is more than just a consumer story - what BEL is doing is essentially depriving children of their dreams. We should be able to get a confront.
